title: Goodman and others copying; black musicians' view
summary: He says black musicians did not mind being copied and liked the competition.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Both reasons that you enjoyed working with Louis Russell. That was the time that Benny Goodman and some of the white players were doing a lot of stealing?
Practically every night.

You mentinned a couple of times ago that Benny Goodman was coming up and at that time he couldn't play jazz at all, but a little later he was beginning to get it together. How did the black musicians feel about Benny Goodman and the rest of them coming up and stealing?
They didn't mind.
They didn't mind?
No, they loved to play. They said, let's play this and see. Try to pick up on this.
How did they feel -
When you got competition you go more. Everybody knows that you are best...
How did they feel about it later on when Benny Goodman was making a lot of money playing the things -
They're not going to tell you.
But they didn't like it?
They loved it. That's where they got their money from. They came in here and copied what we played.
How did the black musicians feel about Benny Goodman making a great deal of money, becoming very famous -
They didn't mind. I didn't hear nobody squawking. We liked it.
(NOT CLEAR)
You sit down and play. You listen to a musician, 'Hey, man, let's put a couple of notes on there. See if we can catch up with this.'
And they did catch up with it and you say the black musicians were happy to have Benny Goodman steal their phrases from them?
There's no other way. You can't take it away. If I hear you play, you cannot stop me. You in the other room and I'm in here listening. You can't stop me from listening.
Didn't they feel that they should be making this money instead of Benny Goodman?
I don't know how they felt.
